equations: BASE_SPENDING = payBase + nonPensionBenefits + PENSIONS + DEBT_INT + defence + central + residualPurchases
Opening pay × reference wage index × (policy output / reference output)^selected pass-through × NI population-volume factor. Public pay therefore responds to the chosen output premium.
Opening component × own real-rate index × NI population-volume factor
PENSIONS × own real-rate index × NI over-65-volume factor × Republic funding share
Defence and central allocations × purchases index × resident volume × unretained share
phase × positive difference between indexed Republic target and indexed NI baseline, separately for gross pay and welfare
net harmonisation = gross harmonisation × source net envelope / source gross envelope. Recovery is counted once, not added again to receipts.
Allocated component spending − baseline receipts − accepted revenue adjustment + net harmonisation + additional expenditure + duplication + service costs − extra receipts + transition interest

Matched GDP concepts. Both frozen 2023 GDP anchors are nowcast to common 2024 using reference NI growth and Republic growth, then scenario growth and official population paths apply. Not PPP, household income, GNI* or a welfare comparison.
Opening transition debt earns interest. Surpluses repay debt then accumulate cash. Fund draws affect financing rather than underlying spending.

Base time is an illustrative 2024 demographic normalisation, using frozen historical fiscal envelopes in 2023 prices. Year t GNI* denominator grows for t years. Not a calendar-year official fiscal forecast.

assumptions: No economic growth is attributed causally to constitutional change.
Historical component allocations are synthetic normalisations, not fresh official programme budgets.
Real pay, welfare and purchases growth defaults are illustrative 1% sensitivities, not forecasts.
Pension headcount uses 65+ population as a proxy. Occupational pensions, retirement ages and cohort rights are not individually modelled.
No inherited debt principal or bond maturity schedule is estimated. Duration of its interest flow is explicitly selected.
Migration stays at the official projection assumptions and is not endogenously driven by the selected growth rate.
GDP includes multinational effects and is not a household living-standard measure. A crossover is flagged, not capped.
Existing sovereign debt and financing feedback are not modelled, so debt/GNI* does not certify affordability.
